newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money rates end lower, gilts inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money rates end lower, gilts inactive.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday lower at 4.00-4.25 percent against the day's opening quotes of 4.00-5.00 percent, dealers said.
"There were some stray deals at 5.25 percent," a dealer at state-run bank said. "Some unexpected demand in mid-session trade took the rates to 5.00 percent but they eased up towards close," he said.

"Today's repo auction will decide the call rates for the rest of the week, while Thursday's 10-year government bond will decide the yield structure for the medium to long maturity paper," the dealer added.
The Reserve Bank of India holds a repo auction of government of India securities later on Wednesday and a 10 billion rupee auction of 10-year government of India securities on Thursday.
Market participants said they expected the cut-off at the repo auction to be between 4.90 and five percent and between 13.60 percent and 13.65 percent for the 10-year bond.
Dealers said there was little selling interest in long-term securities as market participants anticipate an appreciation in their holdings after the 10-year bond auction.
The activity in the securities market was mainly in the short and medium term maturity stocks on Wednesday and prices were steady, dealers said.
The 12.50 percent 2004 stock rose to 96.30 rupees from its last traded price of 96.23 while the 13.50 percent 1997 stock fell to 102.93 rupees from 102.88, dealers said.
Traded volumes were down to 1.21 billion rupees from 2.76 billion, they said.
